subject: IR plan / evidence request: log sampling, redaction criteria, and post-incident package
messages:
From: Alexei Novak <security@fintegrity.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintegrity.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: IR plan + sample evidence following recent notify

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the heads-up earlier on the transient auth failures in eu-west-1. Our SOC team needs the following to close the ticket on our side and to satisfy our internal auditors:

- The latest Incident Response Plan (IRP) snapshot you run against customers (PDF or Drive link).
- A short post-incident summary for the event on 2026-12-09 (what happened, impact, mitigations).
- A small set of telemetry samples (redacted) showing the request/error traces and relevant audit logs for 09 Dec 2026 01:00-03:00 UTC.
- Clarify your redaction rules: what PII, user identifiers, and request payload fields you will strip before handing logs to a customer.

We understand you might have internal controls; if possible, send the IRP and a proposed redaction checklist so we can crosswalk it with our SIG matrix. Ideally we can get a first pass by EOD Friday (2026-12-11) so our procurement review can proceed.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we want to move to a renewal discussion but need this cleared first.

Best,
Alexei Novak
Director, Security Operations
Fintegrity

P.S. If you prefer a quick call for the walk-through, Laura and I are available 11:00-13:00 PST tomorrow.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>
To: Alexei Novak <security@fintegrity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintegrity.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: IR plan + sample evidence following recent notify

Alexei — thanks for the clear list. We ran an internal triage overnight and confirmed the event was a partial KV cache invalidation caused by a control-plane race during a routine rollout; no authentication credentials were exfiltrated and no customer data left our environment. We'll share a short post-incident summary and the IRP snapshot.

Quick notes on the asks and next steps:
- IRP: attaching our current external-facing IRP (redwood_irp_v1.4.pdf). This is our customer-facing runbook (summary + escalation paths).
- Post-incident summary: we'll draft a 1-page timeline and RCA and share it by EOD Friday.
- Telemetry samples: we can provide filtered traces and audit rows. To protect other customers, we do sampling + redaction; we will provide a tarball with placeholders where identifiers were removed. We need Fintegrity to confirm the exact fields you require preserved for your audit (for example, timestamps, request IDs, and high-level model IDs) — anything that could be mapped back to a specific end-user must remain redacted.
- Redaction criteria: attached below is our standard redaction checklist (inline summary in the post below). If you have special requests (e.g., preserve truncated user_id hash) call it out and we can evaluate.

Would a quick 30-min screen share tomorrow at 11:30 PST work to run through the IRP and the redaction checklist? Marissa (sec ops) and Ben (forensics) will join.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Security Liaison, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_irp_v1.4.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Alexei Novak <security@fintegrity.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintegrity.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: IR plan + sample evidence following recent notify

Thanks Sean — that helps. 11:30 PST tomorrow for a walkthrough is good. Two quick clarifications before the call:

1) For the telemetry sample we need the following preserved: timestamps (UTC), request_id, service-component names, error codes, and truncated model_id (first 8 chars only). We do NOT need any user payload or full user identifiers (please remove or hash).
2) Regarding redaction: can you confirm whether request payloads are stored in plaintext in any backup? If so, we need to understand retention and the encryption-at-rest controls for the backup store.

If you can share the filtered telemetry tarball ahead of the call that would speed the call — we can sign an access agreement if needed. Our procurement team will accept a limited PDF extract if the raw archive is sensitive.

See you on the call.

Alexei

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>
To: Alexei Novak <security@fintegrity.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintegrity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: IR plan + sample evidence following recent notify

Alexei / Laura — thanks again for the time earlier. Follow-up from the walkthrough and the artifacts we discussed: 

1) Post-incident one-pager (inline summary):
- Incident window: 2026-12-09 01:11:22 UTC — 2026-12-09 01:43:07 UTC
- Trigger: control-plane rollout race triggered partial KV cache invalidation causing elevated 5xx on non-critical metadata fetch path.
- Impact: 4.2% of ingest requests for a ten-minute window experienced transient errors; all requests retried successfully within client-side retry windows. No data exfiltration or unauthorized access identified.
- Mitigation: rapid rollback of rollout, cache rebuild, and increase in rollout gate checks.
- Follow-ups: extended rollout gating, improved telemetry alert thresholds, and additional canary coverage for cache control paths.

2) Evidence package: we uploaded a filtered sample tar.gz to our secure transfer folder. File: filtered-telemetry-sample-20261210.tar.gz (contains truncated request ids and hashed user_ids; clear timestamps and error codes preserved). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cIRP (permission: Fintegrity-security@fintegrity.com granted).

3) Redaction checklist (summary):
- Remove or hash: full user identifiers, IP addresses, full emails, and any free-text request payloads that could contain PII.
- Preserve: UTC timestamps, request_id (truncated to first 12 chars), service_component, model_id (first 8 chars only), error_code, retry_count.
- Backups: we do not store request payloads in plaintext in long-term backups. Short-lived snapshots exist for 7 days and are encrypted at rest with customer-key integration available for Dedicated/Private customers.

4) Attachments: redwood_irp_v1.4.pdf (customer-facing IRP) and the filtered telemetry tarball (referenced above).

If you need any additional artifacts (S3 access logs, KMS key policy snippet), Marissa can provision scoped extracts. Ben is available for any forensic questions about hashing/redaction choices.

Next actions: please confirm receipt and whether the packaged artifacts meet your SIG/SOC2 evidence requirements. If anything is missing, tell us the exact fields and we will iterate.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Security Liaison | Redwood Inference

Attachments: filtered-telemetry-sample-20261210.tar.gz (application/gzip)
